title: VR Project Brings Hope to Kids in Japan Hospitals
paragraphs: Children who are being treated for cancer often spend a long time in hospital, and some of them do not fully understand what is happening to their bodies. Now, a hospital in Japan has created a virtual reality (VR) game to help them.

In April 2026, Hiroshima University Hospital announced that it had finished making the software, called "Cells at Work! VR." It is based on "Cells at Work!", a popular Japanese manga and anime series in which the cells in the human body, such as red and white blood cells, are shown as characters with their own personalities.

In the VR game, children enter their own bodies as the main characters of the story. In a 360-degree world, they fight bacteria and cancer cells together with white blood cells, and they defeat the cancer cells using anticancer drugs. The game has four episodes, including battles and quizzes about how cells work, and it lasts about 30 minutes. Seven voice actors from the anime voice the characters.
The hospital spent more than three years developing the software. The project was paid for partly by the public, with 132 donations totaling more than 15 million yen.

The aim is to help children see the cells in their bodies as friends who are working for them. According to Dr. Isamu Saeki, who supervised the project, children will understand that their cells are fighting cancer by having fun while playing. Saeki hopes this will help children feel more positive about their treatment.
More than 2,000 children in Japan are diagnosed with cancer each year. The software is expected to be made available to hospitals across Japan that treat children with cancer.
